```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

visits = pd.read_csv("data/visits.csv")
att = pd.read_csv("data/attractions.csv")
w = visits.pivot(index="attraction", columns="year", values="visits")
ratio = (w[2025] / w[2019]).sort_values()
tot19, tot25 = int(w[2019].sum()), int(w[2025].sum())
att["group"] = att["admission"].str.replace(r" \(.*\)", "", regex=True)
grp = att.groupby("group")["visits_2025"].agg(["count", "sum"])
```

# Introduction

Visits to London's attractions fell sharply in 2020 and have since recovered at different speeds. We ask how visits in 2025 compare with 2019 for five major sights, and how 2025 visits differ by admission type, using ALVA member counts [@alva2025; @alva2019].

# Methods

The unit of analysis is an attraction. Visits are annual counts reported by ALVA for its member attractions only, from `data/visits.csv` (2019 and 2025) and `data/attractions.csv` (2025). We compute the ratio of 2025 to 2019 visits per attraction and group the ten attractions in 2025 by admission type as recorded in the data. Counts are not adjusted for changes in what each site counts (see the `note` column).

# Results

Across the five sights the 2025 total is `{python} f"{tot25:,}"` visits against `{python} f"{tot19:,}"` in 2019, a ratio of `{python} f"{tot25/tot19:.2f}"` [@alva2025; @alva2019]. The lowest ratio is `{python} f"{ratio.iloc[0]:.2f}"` (`{python} ratio.index[0]`) and the highest is `{python} f"{ratio.iloc[-1]:.2f}"` (`{python} ratio.index[-1]`) (@fig-recovery).

```{python}
#| label: fig-recovery
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Visits in 2025 as a share of visits in 2019, five London attractions (ALVA member counts)."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the ratio of 2025 to 2019 visits for five London attractions."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
ax.barh(ratio.index, ratio.values)
ax.axvline(1, color="black", lw=1)
ax.set_xlabel("Visits 2025 / visits 2019")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

By admission type in 2025 [@alva2025], the ten attractions split as follows (@tbl-admission).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-admission
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Attractions and visits in 2025 by admission type (ALVA member attractions)."
from IPython.display import Markdown
g = grp.reset_index()
Markdown("| Admission | Attractions | Visits 2025 |\n|:--|--:|--:|\n" + "\n".join(f"| {r.group} | {r['count']} | {int(r['sum']):,} |" for _, r in g.iterrows()))
```

# Conclusions

Visits in 2025 compare with 2019 at the ratios above, and `{python} f"{grp.loc['Free','sum']/grp['sum'].sum():.0%}"` of the 2025 visits to the ten attractions were to attractions with free general admission. These are descriptive counts for ALVA members; they do not show why the ratios differ.
